3: ## Design decisions
4: 
5: - `interleave` accepts two finite iterable inputs and returns a new list, with generic type hints supporting different item types.
6: - Consume one left item, then one right item. Once either iterator ends, append the other iterator's remainder in order.
7: - Use iterator exhaustion rather than a sentinel value, so every input value, including `None`, is preserved.
8: - Input collections are not mutated; iterator inputs are consumed. Items are retained by reference rather than copied.
9: - The implementation uses Python 3.11-compatible standard library features. Runtime and output storage are linear in the total number of items.
10: - Six unittest methods cover equal lengths, both longer-input cases, empty inputs, input preservation/new result allocation, and mixed iterable/item types.
